title: auth: unify project/org key semantics, scoped tokens, nonce signing, and CORS for OpenAI-compat endpoints
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Motivation: We have multiple slightly-different auth/header behaviors across the Redwood API and the OpenAI-compatibility proxy. This has caused developer confusion and a couple of streaming/auth regressions in browser SDKs. This PR unifies semantics for: project and org API keys, scoped short-lived tokens, optional request signing via X-Redwood-Nonce and X-Redwood-Signature, and CORS preflight headers for browser usage with the OpenAI-compat endpoints. It also includes small streaming stability fixes that interact closely with header parsing and connection handoff. Summary of changes: consolidated header parsing into a single auth middleware; introduced explicit precedence rules (Authorization Bearer > X-Redwood-Project-Key > X-Redwood-Org-Key > X-Redwood-Scoped-Token); added support for X-Redwood-Nonce + X-Redwood-Signature for signed requests and a permissive-but-audited fallback for unsigned tokens; updated CORS handling for streaming endpoints and preflight checks (Access-Control-Allow-Credentials and exposed headers); extended openai-compat layer to accept project/org keys and scoped tokens and to translate header semantics to internal auth; added integration tests for streaming + auth combos across browser and server flows; docs update and SDK example snippets for Python/TS. Compatibility notes: default precedence preserves existing bearer token behaviour; scoped tokens are opt-in and require customer configuration to issue; introducing nonce/signature headers is additive - not breaking - but recommend rollout guidance in release notes. See SECURITY section for signing usage and risk model. Checklist: [x] middleware consolidation and unit tests, [x] openai-compat translation, [x] CORS preflight updates for streaming, [x] integration tests for streaming auth variants, [x] docs and SDK examples, [x] performance sanity check on header parsing path. Related: ENG-1987 (auth consolidation), SEC-453 (signing RFC), SUP-321 (customer report about streaming auth in browser).

review_comments: Evelyn Park: Please clarify the precedence ordering in the middleware docs; what happens if both Authorization and X-Redwood-Scoped-Token are present?
Sofia Martinez (author): Precedence is Authorization Bearer -> X-Redwood-Project-Key -> X-Redwood-Org-Key -> X-Redwood-Scoped-Token. Updated docs to reflect and added unit test verifying the order.
Ravi Patel: The CORS change exposing headers looks fine but double-checks needed for credentialed requests from browsers; we shouldn't relax wildcard origins here.

Sofia Martinez: Correct, we kept existing origin checking and only adjusted Access-Control-Expose-Headers and Access-Control-Allow-Credentials for streaming endpoints. Added an integration test against a strict origin set.
Lena Hoffman: The signing scaffold looks good but we need a migration plan for customers who may opt into nonce enforcement. Add a feature flag and a metric to track rejected signed requests.
Sofia Martinez: Added deploy flag (redwood.enable_nonce_enforcement) and a metric redwood.auth.signed_reject_count; documented rollout guidance in the SECURITY section of the PR description.
Evelyn Park: CI failed on lint initially - good to see fixes. Approving after addressing comments.
Ravi Patel: Verified integration test passes locally. Approving.
Lena Hoffman: Approved and left note to follow up in SEC-453 for hardened signature verification algorithms.

merge_outcome: Merged by Evelyn Park via squash-and-merge on 2026-02-24. Merge commit message: 'auth: unify header semantics for project/org/scoped tokens, add nonce signing and CORS fixes (ENG-1987, SEC-453)'.
release_notes: Auth/header semantics: unified precedence across API and OpenAI-compat layer. New headers supported: X-Redwood-Project-Key, X-Redwood-Org-Key, X-Redwood-Scoped-Token, X-Redwood-Nonce, X-Redwood-Signature. CORS: streaming endpoints now expose X-Redwood-* headers for browser SDKs and support credentialed requests from configured origins. Scoped tokens and nonce/signature are opt-in features; see docs/openai-compat/auth.md for rollout and migration guidance.
notes_for_ops: Ops: a new deploy flag 'redwood.enable_nonce_enforcement' toggles strict nonce signature enforcement. Default is false; metric redwood.auth.signed_reject_count added under metrics/ingest. Recommend enabling in staging, monitoring signed_reject_count for 48h, then enable in production for customers who opt in.
security_notes: Signing is provided as an additional anti-replay/anti-forgery layer. Implementation uses per-request nonces and HMAC signature verification when enforcement is enabled. Customers should rotate signing keys regularly; we document key management and KMS integration in docs. Any customer who enables nonce enforcement should also ensure clock skew allowances are accounted for.
examples_added: Python example: show project-key + X-Redwood-Nonce signing for server-to-server calls
TS browser example: show how to use scoped short-lived tokens and refresh flow while keeping credentials out of long-lived storage
